title: Nemrut Dağ tumulus
summary: Nemrut Dağ in south-east Turkey is the hilltop temple-tomb of King Antiochos I of Commagene, who ruled 69-34 BCE. A mound of stone chips about 50 metres high and 145 metres across crowns the summit, with terraces on three sides carrying giant seated statues of gods. Weathering and visitors have lowered it from an estimated 60 metres.

uncertainty.note: The pages date the monument to the reign of Antiochos I (69-34 BCE) without a construction year; start is the first year of the reign (astronomical -68) and the build may fall anywhere up to -33. End is the present.

phases.description: Built by Antiochos I of Commagene (69-34 BCE) as a temple-tomb for himself; the pages give no construction year.
The mound is now reduced from its estimated original 60 m by weathering, uncontrolled earlier research and climbing by visitors.

reviewer_note: Shape mound. Least sure of the date: the pages give only the reign of Antiochos I (69-34 BCE), so the construction phase spans the reign and the altered phase start (-33) is not a dated event. Diameter 145 m (UNESCO) vs 150 m (ICOMOS); height 50 m now vs estimated 60 m originally. Point is the Nemrut Dağı peak node in OSM.
